entries.note: Marcus speculates that LeCun probably reached his conclusions honestly after recognizing failures. The proposition removes that hedge and generalizes who recognizes them.

entries.test: Public research and evaluations establishing whether language-only training can produce general cognitive abilities comparable to human intelligence would test the claimed limitation.
entries.note: The categorical formulation is attributed to LeCun and Browning. Marcus explicitly endorses their argument and presents it as matching his own earlier position.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and independent evaluations of whether large language models alone achieve artificial general intelligence would test the asserted limitation.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies a plain reading of “solve AI”: achieve general intelligence.

entries.test: Public experiments testing whether language models lack robust representations of unfolding events and whether supplying those representations remedies their failures would test the causal claim.
entries.note: The surrounding passage explains cognitive models through robust representations of how events unfold over time.
Marcus endorses cognitive models as a critical research priority in pursuing general intelligence. The proposition broadens this into a requirement for AI systems generally.
Calling the proposal well-motivated, alongside saying he has advocated it himself, endorses the recommendation.
